expected_effect: Direction: public_val_bpb lower than same-host control. Size: steps +15% to +30% vs control (2380-2700 on trn21; 2390-2700 on trn22) with per-step quality within noise of control, giving public_val_bpb 0.995-1.002 (i.e. 0.004-0.011 below control). SUCCESS threshold: steps >= +10% and BPB <= control - 0.002. Falsification: steps within +/-2% of control (block FP32 matmuls not the cost), or steps >= +10% with BPB >= control (the 0.0105 regression is inside the block projections rather than the head path; recorded alongside the full-policy 2716 / 1.016279 row for attribution).
hypothesis: At 9a4caa7b the --bf16-norm-output flag (KEEP-quality-failed row al-20260922-bf16-norm-output-policy-r3-full-r1: 2716 steps vs 2071 control, +31% steps, but public_val_bpb 1.016279 vs 1.005734) shows that FP32 matmuls fed by norm() outputs are the dominant wall-clock cost of the default configuration, while the 0.0105 BPB regression shows at least one BF16 norm-output site damages learning enough to erase a 31% step gain. The same flag casts EVERY norm() output to BF16, including the final norm whose output enters the LM head (so the head weight is taken from the BF16 cache in Linear.forward and the logits are produced in BF16 before .float()/softcap/CE) and any non-block norms. I hypothesize the throughput gain lives almost entirely in the two per-block projection boundaries (pre-attention norm -> qkv/local-conv path, pre-MLP norm -> MLP up-projection; 6 blocks, ~42M of the 55.7M dense parameters) while the quality loss is concentrated in the final-norm -> head -> logits path. Casting only the two block pre-norm outputs to BF16 and leaving the final norm, head and all other norm sites exactly as in the control should retain most of the step gain (predicted +15..30% steps) without the quality regression, yielding a lower fixed-budget public_val_bpb than the control. Comparison against both the same-host control and the recorded full-policy run gives attribution either way: if BPB stays ~1.016 the regression is in the block projections, not the head.

single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: a new module-level toggle USE_BF16_BLOCK_NORM_OUTPUT (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_BLOCK_NORM_OUTPUT='0' disables; CLI --bf16-block-norm-output/--no-bf16-block-norm-output; added to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES so checkpoints persist it and load_for_eval restores it) makes exactly two norm() outputs per transformer Block BF16 -- the pre-attention norm output (the tensor that enters the attention input projection path, including any local-conv that precedes the qkv projection) and the pre-MLP norm output (the tensor that enters the MLP up-projection) -- using the identical cast expression the existing --bf16-norm-output policy applies. Every other norm() output (final norm before the LM head, QK norms, ngram-ve/rms, out-pool, head-gate, sandwich or any other norm site) keeps its current default-flag dtype (FP32), so the LM head continues to consume FP32 activations and the FP32 master weight, and logits/softcap/CE/eval/causality code paths are untouched. No --bf16-norm-output, no --bf16-sdpa-input, no other precision, kernel, optimizer, schedule, batch, architecture or evaluator change; num_params_M must remain 592.9 and all config oneliners must be identical to control except one new field. Launch smoke and full with the exact control command/environment (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42; NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) and no additional flags. Full-run classification vs same-host pinned control (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967), evaluated in order: (1) HALT-INERT if static inspection finds the two block pre-norm outputs are already BF16 under default flags (no patch, no run); (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-2% of control (block-projection FP32 matmuls are not the dominant cost); (4) SUCCESS if steps >= +10% of control and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.002; (5) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +10% and public_val_bpb >= control (the regression is inside the block projections; attribution note: compare to bf16-norm-output-policy-r3 2716 / 1.016279 on trn21); (6) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (steps +2..10%, or >= +10% with a gain smaller than 0.002). Verdicts use only the fixed-budget public_val_bpb; smoothed training-loss logs are attribution notes, not validation BPB.
